about: bank 1 $6018-$6FFF: bank 1's side of the cross-bank table, a copy of bank 0's library (math box set-up, shifts, unit vector helpers, sine, BCD, random, sound command stubs), the view routine of the title logo and the logo's outline data

B1:61FD.name: asrd12_b1
B1:61FD.desc: bank 1's copy of asrd12: arithmetic shift right of D by 12 bits, done as a byte move, sign extension and 4 shifts of B. first of five such entries (12 to 8 bits) in front of Atari's ASRD chain. no caller found in bank 1, unused as far as can be seen

B1:6205.name: asrd11_b1
B1:6205.desc: bank 1's copy of asrd11: arithmetic shift right of D by 11 bits. no caller found, unused as far as can be seen

B1:620C.name: asrd10_b1
B1:620C.desc: bank 1's copy of asrd10: arithmetic shift right of D by 10 bits. no caller found, unused as far as can be seen

B1:6212.name: asrd9_b1
B1:6212.desc: bank 1's copy of asrd9: arithmetic shift right of D by 9 bits. no caller found, unused as far as can be seen

B1:6217.name: asrd8_b1
B1:6217.desc: bank 1's copy of asrd8: arithmetic shift right of D by 8 bits, A to B and sign extend. no caller found, unused as far as can be seen. the two bytes after its RTS are the ASRD7 entry of the chain that follows

B1:6227.desc: entry point: arithmetic shift D right 1 bit, then the RTS at ASRD0_B1. called at KE8BE

B1:622A.name: lsrd12_b1
B1:622A.desc: bank 1's copy of lsrd12: logical shift right of D by 12 bits, A to B, clear A, 4 shifts of B. first of the logical shift right library (12 to 8 bits as short routines, then the chain at lsrd7_b1). no caller found for any of them in bank 1

B1:6232.name: lsrd11_b1
B1:6232.desc: bank 1's copy of lsrd11: logical shift right of D by 11 bits. no caller found, unused as far as can be seen

B1:6239.name: lsrd10_b1
B1:6239.desc: bank 1's copy of lsrd10: logical shift right of D by 10 bits. no caller found, unused as far as can be seen

B1:623F.name: lsrd9_b1
B1:623F.desc: bank 1's copy of lsrd9: logical shift right of D by 9 bits. no caller found, unused as far as can be seen

B1:6244.name: lsrd8_b1
B1:6244.desc: bank 1's copy of lsrd8: logical shift right of D by 8 bits, A to B and clear A. no caller found, unused as far as can be seen

B1:6248.name: lsrd7_b1
B1:6248.desc: logical shift right of D by 7 bits: seven LSRA RORB pairs and an RTS, the fall-through chain whose 4 bit entry is lsrd4 in bank 0 (there the first three pairs are listed as data at LB2FC). the entries for 6 to 1 bits are every two bytes inside it. no caller of any of them was found in bank 1

B1:6257.name: lsld12_b1
B1:6257.desc: bank 1's copy of lsld12: shift D left 12 bits, B to A, clear B, 4 shifts of A. first of five such entries (12 to 8 bits) in front of Atari's LSLD chain. no caller found, unused as far as can be seen

B1:625F.name: lsld11_b1
B1:625F.desc: bank 1's copy of lsld11: shift D left 11 bits. no caller found, unused as far as can be seen

B1:6266.name: lsld10_b1
B1:6266.desc: bank 1's copy of lsld10: shift D left 10 bits. no caller found, unused as far as can be seen

B1:626C.name: lsld9_b1
B1:626C.desc: bank 1's copy of lsld9: shift D left 9 bits. no caller found, unused as far as can be seen

B1:6271.name: lsld8_b1
B1:6271.desc: bank 1's copy of lsld8: shift D left 8 bits, B to A and clear B. no caller found, unused as far as can be seen. the ten bytes after its RTS are the LSLD7 to LSLD3 entries of the chain that follows

B1:62B1.name: tranu1_entry_b1
B1:62B1.desc: bank 1's copy of tranu1_entry, the real entry of ESB's TRANU1: it saves U, which the transpose uses as its second scratch register, and the code ends with PULS U,PC. the TRANU1_B1 label two bytes further on must not be called by itself. no call to either address was found in bank 1

B1:62D9.name: store_u1_blk_b1
B1:62D9.desc: bank 1's copy of store_u1_block: copies the ship 1 download block of the math box (the nine matrix terms, the three spare words and the position) into the unit vector block whose middle U points at. no caller found in bank 1

B1:633D.name: presub_via_u2_b1
B1:633D.desc: bank 1's copy of presub_via_u2: swaps the ship 1 and ship 2 download blocks, runs math box program $67 for the block index in M_BIC and waits, then swaps the blocks back. no caller found in bank 1

B1:6349.name: swap_u1_u2_b1
B1:6349.desc: bank 1's copy of swap_u1_u2: exchanges the ship 1 download block with the ship 2 block word by word, the nine matrix terms and the position. U is saved and used as the second scratch register. the three headers that follow are parts of this one routine. called only by presub_via_u2_b1

B1:6357.name: swap_u1_u2_b1_b
B1:6357.desc: not a separate routine and not TRANU1: swap_u1_u2_b1 continues here with the A.Y word. no call or jump to this address was found

B1:639F.name: swap_u1_u2_b1_c
B1:639F.desc: not a separate routine: swap_u1_u2_b1 continues here with the C.Y word. no call or jump to this address was found

B1:63B7.name: swap_u1_u2_b1_d
B1:63B7.desc: not a separate routine: swap_u1_u2_b1 ends here with the three position words and PULS U,PC. no call or jump to this address was found

B1:63FE.name: roll_by_angle_b1
B1:63FE.desc: bank 1's copy of roll_by_angle: B = angle (256 to the full turn), block index already in M_BIC. sets M_SIN and M_COS from the sine table and runs math box program MS_ROLL. no caller found in bank 1

B1:6406.name: pitch_by_angle_b1
B1:6406.desc: bank 1's copy of pitch_by_angle: as roll_by_angle_b1 with math box program MS_PTCH. no caller found in bank 1

B1:640E.name: yaw_by_angle_b1
B1:640E.desc: bank 1's copy of yaw_by_angle: as roll_by_angle_b1 with math box program MS_YAW. no caller found in bank 1

B1:6416.name: set_sin_cos_b1
B1:6416.desc: bank 1's copy of set_sin_cos: B = angle (256 to the full turn), writes its sine to M_SIN and its cosine to M_COS for the math box rotate programs. X is saved, D returns the cosine. used only by the three unused rotate entries in front of it

B1:642E.name: sine_b1
B1:642E.desc: bank 1's copy of sine: B = angle (256 to the full turn), returns D = sine as a signed fraction with $4000 = 1.0. looks the first quadrant up in the 65-word table sine_tab_b1, reads the table backwards for the second quadrant and negates the value for angles $80-$FF. uses X

B1:6511.name: rnd_set_b1
B1:6511.desc: bank 1's copy of rnd_set, ESB's form of the Star Wars RND8: moves RND_S1 and RND_S2 down to RND_S3 and the byte after it, then reads two new bytes from the pokey random register P_RND1 into RND_S2 and RND_S1. called by the star code at K7D0F and K7D50

B1:66D0.name: view_title_logo
B1:66D0.desc: ESB's VWBNNR, rewritten: views the title of the banner phase, called once a frame by PHEBNR through the cross-bank entry L60F0 with Y = display list pointer. counts BN_CNT up. for the first $20 frames the logo brightens in place (bn_brite up 5 a frame, linear scale $20), then it dims by 2 a frame and shrinks (linear scale up 3 a frame) towards a point 358 units above the screen centre, and from frame $68 it is not drawn. the logo is 27 outlines listed in ttl_outline_tab, each drawn by title_outline: the first six, STAR WARS, in colour 1 and the others, THE EMPIRE STRIKES BACK and two bars, in colour 3. where Star Wars called six vector ROM pictures, ESB builds the vectors from point lists. ends by jumping to bank 0's spmess_entry, the special messages part of the Star Wars routine

B1:6791.name: title_outline
B1:6791.desc: draws one outline of the title logo: U = list of 5-byte records (flag byte, x word, y word, a flag of 0 ends the list), Y = display list pointer. the pen starts at x 0, y $198. for each record it writes a long vector from the last point to this one, blank when bit 0 of the flag is set (flag 1) and at intensity 7 otherwise (flag 2). called only by view_title_logo

4C03.name: bn_scale
4C03.desc: word: scale instruction of the title logo drawn by bank 1's view_title_logo, $72 and the linear scale. Star Wars' BN_SCL at a new address

4C04.name: bn_scale_lo
4C04.desc: low byte of bn_scale, the logo's linear scale: $20 while the logo brightens, then up 3 a frame to $F8 at most, which shrinks it away

4803.name: tmp_prev_y
4803.desc: temp of title_outline in bank 1 (word): y of the last point of the outline being drawn. the address is a shared temp of many routines (TMPDY, TMPOCT, TMPSIZ, TMPTP3 in Star Wars)

4805.name: tmp_inten
4805.desc: temp of title_outline in bank 1: intensity bits for the vector being written, $E0 to draw or 0 to move. the address is a shared temp (TMPXD in Star Wars)

questions: B1:67C9-$712A - this block is not a script like the rebel training manual: it is the 27 point lists of the title logo that view_title_logo (K66D0) draws through the pointer table at K675B. the records are 5 bytes (flag, x word, y word), so no region kind fits and the listing will keep them as .byte rows of 8. it would read better as one record per line. the block ends at $712A, past my range: the lists at K7014 (A of BACK), K7056 (C), K70C0 (K) and K7111 (the underline bar, 4 corners) and the tail of the B at K6F73-K7013 belong to the next stretch and have no labels from me

which outline is which letter i took from a plot of the points and from the point counts, not from running the game. the six STAR WARS outlines are the least certain: by position 0 is ST, 1 W, 2 and 3 the two As, 4 the R of STAR and 5 the RS of WARS, with three of them drawn out into the frame around the other words
B1:66D0 has no routine header in the snapshot (it follows aud_cmd_52_b1 without a break) although it is the target of the table entry K60F3. i gave it a routines entry

B1:621B - the two bytes $47,$56 shown as data are code: ASRA RORB, the ASRD7 entry. B1:6275 - the ten bytes $58,$49 x5 are code: LSLB ROLA five times, the LSLD7 to LSLD3 entries. nothing calls them, as in bank 0 (B0:B2FC)

B1:6357, B1:639F, B1:63B7 - these headers split swap_u1_u2_b1 at addresses nothing refers to, as B0:B40B, B0:B453 and B0:B46B do in bank 0, where 00_start lists them under no_header. the name TRANU1_B1_2 at B1:6357 is a false match (i put it in sw_drop_names): the code swaps the ship 1 and ship 2 blocks, it does not transpose. B1:62B3 TRANU1_B1 is the real transpose but its entry is K62B1 (PSHS U)

most of this library has no caller in bank 1 and cannot be called from bank 0 or the slapstic pages: IPGEN_B1, IMATH_B1, IS1UV_B1, S1RL_B1, S1PT_B1, S1YW_B1, BCDBIN_B1, AUDTST_B1, PMTST_B1, all the spk_cmd and tune_cmd stubs and all aud_cmd stubs but $38, $3B and $3F (called at KE325-KE360). what bank 1 does call: MGOWT_B1, UNITV_B1, IS2UV_B1, BINBCD, rnd_set_b1 (K6511), ASRD6_B1, ASRD5, ASRD4, ASRD1_B1 and LSLD2. it looks like the same library source assembled into both banks

the table comments at B1:60A5-B1:61B3 describe routines outside my range from a short look at each and at their bank 0 callers. the annotators of $7000-$7FFF and $D000-$EFFF should correct them where they know better. entries with no call found through them from bank 0 or the slapstic pages: L60AE, L60D8, L611A, L6138, L613E, L614A, L6162, L619E
$4803 and $4805 are shared temps with several Star Wars aliases in esb_defines.asm but show as bare operands. i named them after their use in title_outline. the reconciler may prefer one general name

the 22 outline labels from B1:6856 to B1:6F73 and their comments sit at addresses that are in the middle of an 8-byte .byte row in the snapshot. they rely on the generator starting a new row at a label
B1:6751 - the loop of view_title_logo ends when X reaches K6791, the address of the code after the table, so the table has exactly 27 entries
